posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
cool idea for a hero mechanic!

Edit: What if Twitchy is not considered a "hero", but we get to play his deck against the villains along side the proper heros? Something like that could work out thematically at least, since FILTER agents only seem to distinguish between super vs normal instead of the good vs evil mindset of traditional heros. He would not be touched by any attacks that only target hero targets, but would probably have to come with some major draw backs to whatever his powers and abilities would end up being to make that kind of trade off

posts.name: Rabit
posts.cooked:
Yeah, I don't see them doing anything that convoluted/complex. >G is big on using the structure of the game to build interesting possibilities. They tend not to break the fundamentals of the game when designing new components.

I'm guessing Twitchy will be a "normal" hero, but he'll have ongoings that give him really nice, thematically-appropriate abilities/powers, but which also make him count as a villain target or a non-hero target. Also figure he'll have some cards that make him take damage that would normally target lowest hit point or highest hit point hero targets (i.e., he's unlucky).

Looking forward to seeing what they come up with, though!

posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
So, I was thinking more about Twitchy today

I have it in my mind that he is a F.I.L.T.E.R. agent. I have seen other people express the same sentiment. Where did we get this from?

Is it only because of the emblem on his chest resembles the holding cells in the Block? Like the one Unity finds herself in on her incap side? If this is the case, let me pose an alternate theory (if its not, oh well. it was good while it lasted like my freedom wraith = operative idea)

 

I do not think the emblem on his chest is a FILTER prison cell. You know the card in Kismets deck where she is punching Twichy and we see a bunch of Casino/gambling related art?  I think his emblem is a die. This die only has one side with a value on it, and thats what he rolled. He rolled a 1. Snake Eyes.  

Him rolling snake eyes fits thematically with the popular rumor that he is probably just naturally unlucky. This fits in with him getting unluckily zapped by Shock Rounds and also fits within the potential Nemesis dynamic where Kismet is super lucky and Twitchy can't roll anything but the figurative "snake eyes". If he can not help but be unlucky, then we see another Nemesis dynamic take shape in the form of Infinite Possibilities vs Fixed Outcomes. Kismet's luck can potentially make anything happen if she just gets "lucky" enough. With Twitchy it is the exact opposite. His outcomes, possibly his entire destiny, are set in stone, fated to happen the same way every time. When he rolls a die, it will always be 1.

Plot wise, this puts him in a very unique situation as it pertains to "the multiverse" and the time cataclysm, as he could act as a common thread between them all, potentially being a key to preventing the possible dark futures of Iron Legacy and The Final Wasteland. I also now picture him as having a very bad gambling addiction before gaining his powers

posts.name: Benhimself
posts.cooked:
So I had this idea on how to implement a "bad luck" hero:

Imagine, say, an ongoing that read "Whenever you take damage, every other hero target regains 1 hp" or "whenever you discard one or more cards, every other hero draws a card". A deck that encourages you to take the brunt of the villain and environment's beatdowns, or possibly even get "accidentally" struck by your teammates (Shock Rounds and Kismet's Jinx destruction I am looking at you), maybe combined with a slightly better than average incapacitated side?

posts.name: Chromium_Man
posts.cooked:
I like that idea but I wonder what the incentive would be for someone to play that character in a non-solo game. 

Along the same lines, what if the bad luck hero was an MMO-style aggro magnet i.e. "Whenever an attack would deal damage to a hero other than [the bad luck hero], deal that damage to [the bad luck hero] instead. He would be a true tank and one can assume that the rest of the deck's mechanics would reflect the fact that a hero whose whole shtick is having horrible luck but whose career lasted more than a week must have some novel ways of staying alive.  

Obviously there'd have to be some stipulations to keep one AOE attack from killing him on the first turn
